Synopsis:
    The US and Venezuela have announced a landmark 25-year oil deal granting Washington control over ~65 billion barrels of recoverable Venezuelan crude across 17 oilfields, primarily in the Orinoco Belt. The deal bypassed competitive tendering and was negotiated secretly. Legal experts question its validity, the tax framework, and the selection process for operating companies. NABEP (linked to Alejandro Betancourt) is reportedly positioned as a key intermediary. Trump framed part of the rationale around replenishing the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve amid Iran conflict-driven gasoline price pressure. Transparency concerns are significant on both sides.
